newsitem.title: USA: U.S. says won backing for Croatia loan delay.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says won backing for Croatia loan delay.

text.p: The World Bank has delayed debate on a $30 million loan to Croatia after complaints from countries worried about Zagreb meeting promises made under the Dayton peace accords, the U.S. State Department said on Tuesday.

Spokesman John Dinger told a news briefing the United States was worried that Croatia had not complied in full with the 1995 Dayton agreement, which ended the Yugoslavia war. He said other countries had backed this view.
"I understand that the (World) Bank board did decide to postpone indefinitely consideration of a $30 million loan to Croatia," he said.
"I understand there was broad multilateral support for that decision in view of Croatia's insufficient compliance with its obligations under the Dayton agreement."
The World Bank first postponed debate on the loan last week after the U.S. complained about Croatia's performance regarding the return of refugees and the handing over of suspected war criminals.

But the credit, designed to strengthen Croatia's banking system, was placed on the agenda for Tuesday's meeting of the World Bank board. Dinger said he believed that the World Bank had decided on Tuesday to postpone consideration of the loan.
World Bank officials were not immediately available for comment.
Dinger said Croatia's failure to meet its Dayton obligations could have wider implications.

"Failure to comply with one international agreement brings into question how it complies with other international agreements," he said. "For example failing to comply with Dayton may have an implication on failing to comply with international financial institutions."
